Sep. 2021 – Mar. 2022

Electromagnetic Simulation and Optimization of a Ferrite Microwave Circulator

Finite-element simulation and structural optimization of a nonreciprocal ferrite microwave device.

  • COMSOL
  • Electromagnetic Simulation
  • Device Optimization

Overview

This project investigated the electromagnetic behavior of a ferrite microwave circulator through three-dimensional finite-element simulation. A parameterized model was developed using the COMSOL RF Module to analyze and optimize nonreciprocal microwave transmission.

Key Work

  • Solved the frequency-domain Maxwell equations with an anisotropic permeability tensor to model gyromagnetic effects under an external bias field.
  • Analyzed electric-field distributions and time-averaged power flow, and performed parametric sweeps using the S-parameters S11, S21, and S31.

Highlight

The optimized design achieved an operating frequency range of 8.8–9.5 GHz and a minimum reflection coefficient of S11 = −43.04 dB.

Publication

Xiao Cao, Cuiqin Bai, et al. “COMSOL Simulation of Ferrite Microwave Circulator.” College Physics, 41(9), 63 (2022). [Link]
